items.title: Godfather Of Cyberpunk Also Hooked On Watching GTA 6 Clips
items.summary: Arcade addicts of the 1980s inspired the cyberspace of William Gibson’s influential Neuromancer, now the author is transfixed on viral footage of Rockstar’s ultra-hit
items.content:
Cyberpunk Grand Theft Auto 6 Neuromancer William Gibson

William Gibson, the science fiction author often credited for establishing the cyberpunk genre, took plenty of inspiration from video game culture in the ’70s and ’80s. Despite this, and the influence of works like Neuromancer has had on the medium, Gibson says he doesn’t partake in the hobby, claiming this weekend that he’s never even played a video game. One game seems to be recapturing his interest, though, the forefather of virtual reality allured by viral Grand Theft Auto clips online.

“I’ve never played a video game in my life, but this thing [ Grand Theft Auto ] actually does [seem] interesting,” posted Gibson . “When I said that I found that clip of the new GTA interesting, I didn’t mean that it made me interested in learning to play it, but interested in what it was that I found intriguing, in some mysterious way, in its…texture?…depth? I don’t know.”

When I said that I found that clip of the new GTA interesting, I didn’t mean that it made me interested in learning to play it, but interested in what it was that I found intriguing, in some mysterious way, in its…texture?…depth? I don’t know.

— William Gibson (@greatdismal.bsky.social) 2026-11-22T03:23:17.866Z

In the early ‘80s, William Gibson released Neuromancer , the first novel in his ‘Sprawl’ series and an establishing work of cyberpunk literature. In it, hackers, mercenaries and ‘street samurai’ orchestrate a heist across cities, planets and virtual realities. Much of the nomenclature around the digital world and the notion of cyberspace come from his works . And much of that world was built through observing teens and drug peddlers looming around Vancouver arcades in the ‘70s, as well as the rapid transformation of computers from fridge-sized number crunchers to desktop work stations .

Despite changing video games forever, and games directly adapted from his works, Gibson hasn’t participated in playing them. Replying to fans stunned he’s never given one a whirl, Gibson says it’s possible he tried Pong , “on a tabletop in a bar?”

Now, like thousands others, Gibson is hooked on amusing clips emerging out of Grand Theft Auto VI . The one kicking off the conversation featuring a boom barrier launching Jason like a catapult to Lucia’s embarrassment. This time from the comfort of homes and phones, people around the world are sitting backseat to endless streams of the new game. Even those who don’t consider themselves players taken in by virtual birdwatchers and infrastructure fanatics .

“I was enthralled by this one streamer pretending to host a nature documentary while wandering around the wilderness of Leonida,” writes Defector ’s Brandy Jensen on being unexpectedly taken in by GTA streams. “I cheered as Jason is, for reasons that remain completely beyond me, rescued by a dog driving a jetski. I even found myself beguiled by the many ways a digitally rendered human body can react to getting hit by a basketball.”

If the early sales figures are true , Grand Theft Auto VI is the highest performing piece of media of all time. The ramifications of which are surreal to wrap your head around, regardless of being an eager fan or a cultural observer. It has even reeled in William Gibson, though he’s still figuring out the words to describe the phenomenon. And once he does, maybe it’ll lay the groundwork for the next century of speculative dystopia.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2 Director Isn’t Trying To Outdo GTA 6, Because That’s Impossible
items.summary: Trying to match a game with the budget and resources of GTA 6 is a fool's errand, and CD Projekt Red understands that.
items.content:
CD Projekt Red Add TheGamer on Google Add as Preferred Source By James Lucas Published Nov 22, 2026, 10:16 AM EST James Lucas is the Lead Photo Editor at TheGamer and has worked in professional journalism since 2018. A Newcastle University graduate with a degree in Journalism, Media, and Culture, they have written hundreds of guides, news stories, and original reports, with bylines in IGN, NME, GaymingMag, and VG247, sourcing interviews with studio heads, legendary industry figures, prominent actors, and more. You can reach them at James.t@thegamer.com Sign in to your TheGamer account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Grand Theft Auto 6 is the highest-rated game in history , only rivaled by Ocarina of Time — but no developer should try to rival its scope and ambition.

We don't know what exactly the budget was, but Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe recently pushed back on rumors of a $2 billion price tag, clarifying it cost somewhere under $1.5 billion. Most studios don't have that kind of change to throw around, because most studios aren't printing money with a game like GTA Online .

Indeed, Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski has made it clear that CD Projekt Red has no intention of rivaling GTA 6, despite the broad-stroke similarities between both series.

"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real," he mused on Bluesky . "Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle. Cyberpunk 2 is canceled, imma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now.

"Seriously though I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor," he continued. "GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed."

It's a sentiment echoed by others in the games' industry, like Larian Studios head of publishing Michael Douse, better known by his online moniker - Very AFK.

"Maybe in a world that often feels like it's going to sh*t it is nice for everyone to enjoy a cultural moment together that brings every audience (and every generation) the same excitement, behind something that has turned out to be genuinely brilliant," he posted to Twitter . "Not every game needs to be GTA, and that both makes space for other types of experiences, and the rare moment even more special!"

Naughty Dog game designer Michael Barclay even said that GTA 6 appears to him "as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child."

Considering, just three years ago, the industry warned that Baldur's Gate 3 was the game no other developer should try to replicate, given the unbelievable scope and sheer amount of interactivity, recorded dialogue, and branching paths it offered to players, that's one hell of an endorsement.

TheGamer's own Lead News Editor, George Foster, put it bluntly in his GTA 6 review, "we'll never get a game like it again," and frankly, we shouldn't.

GTA 6 has reportedly been pre-ordered almost ten millions times.

Ballooning development budgets are already putting a target on studios' backs, making every single new release a financial gamble that could mean mass layoffs or even closure, and those high-stakes are only making the industry increasingly risk-averse.

GTA 6 shouldn't set a new bar for other developers to strive for. The unimaginable amount of resources, personnel, and time it took to develop the game is simply unrealistic for other studios. Thankfully, CDPR understands that. Let's just hope the rest of the industry does, too.

items.content:
Korean (한국어) KO Add us on CDPR G-STAR Booth G-STAR 2026 Location Busan BEXCO Exhibition Center 2 Dates November 19–22 The Witcher 3 Remastered Cyberpunk 2077 Demos Events Merchandise CD Projekt Red has joined G-STAR 2026. At their booth located in Exhibition Center 2 of BEXCO in Busan from November 19 to 22, visitors can get hands-on experience with The Witcher 3 Remastered and Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5. In addition, a Korean-dubbed gameplay video for The Witcher 3's new expansion, Songs of the Past—scheduled for release in 2027—is also on display.

A steady stream of attendees visited CD Projekt Red's booth, forming long queues. With Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 having aired recently, many fans came to soak in the lingering excitement. Cosplayers dressed as characters from the original Cyberpunk: Edgerunners were also frequently spotted. On the 21st, a large group of cosplayers visited the booth and spent a fun time with attendees.

Two playable games were featured at the booth. First, The Witcher 3 Remastered enhances the visual effects, performance, and gameplay of the 2015 original title and its expansions, Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine. At the G-STAR venue, attendees can experience the game hands-on for 20 minutes.

Cyberpunk 2077 is also available to play. In this demo, visitors can play the game running Update 2.5 for 20 minutes, experiencing newly added Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 content alongside various gameplay elements.

Events were also prepared alongside the game demos, allowing visitors to earn various merchandise. Giveaway prizes, including limited-edition figures, are awarded to the first 500 attendees each day who complete a demo session. Additionally, a Cyberpunk: Edgerunners collaboration beverage created in partnership with SPRINT is provided.

The booth's demos and events are open to attendees aged 19 and older, with a limit of up to three entries per person per day. From new Witcher and Cyberpunk content to game demos and merchandise, here is a look in photos at CD Projekt Red's G-STAR 2026 booth.

Xbox's latest free game event includes a 9/10 cyberpunk FPS if GTA isn't your thing
items.summary: Vice City can wait. There's a cyberpunk shooter calling your name 🔫
items.content:
Xbox Free Play Days offers three games this weekend, including Deadlink, a cyberpunk FPS with nearly 90% positive Steam reviews.

GTA VI is finally here, and while everyone and their neighbour's cat is talking about Rockstar Games' latest blockbuster, it might not be everyone's cup of tea. Thankfully, if you're looking for something different to play this weekend, Xbox has announced its latest batch of free games, including a fantastic cyberpunk FPS.

As part of Xbox Free Play Days, eligible Xbox Game Pass subscribers can play three games at no extra cost for a limited time. One of those games is a critically acclaimed first-person shooter with an impressive 91% positive user review rating on Steam, equivalent to roughly 9/10, and it might just be worth checking out if you fancy taking a break from the streets of Vice City.

The Xbox Free Play Days event runs until Sunday November 22, 2026, and requires an Xbox Game Pass Essential, Premium or Ultimate subscription.

One of the highlights of this weekend's Xbox Free Play Days is Deadlink , a fast-paced cyberpunk FPS developed by Gruby Entertainment, which combines high-octane first-person combat with roguelite gameplay.

Set in a dystopian future where powerful corporations rule the world (which might sound familiar to Cyberpunk 2077 fans), players take on the role of an operative tasked with taking down these organisations, using an arsenal of weapons, abilities and upgrades.

Deadlink has also received plenty of praise from critics and the community since its release, including an impressive 9.5/10 from GameGrin, which praised its fast-paced combat and addictive gameplay. So, if you're a fan of games such as DOOM and Cyberpunk 2077 , this might be right up your street.

Of course, Deadlink isn't the only game included in this weekend's Xbox Free Play Days promotion, with two other titles available to play at no extra cost.

Here are all three games included in the latest promotion:

All three games are available to eligible Xbox Game Pass subscribers until Sunday November 22, 2026. Simply head to the Xbox Store, find the Free Play Days collection and download whichever game takes your fancy.

What's more, if you enjoy any of these games enough to purchase them afterwards, you'll be able to carry over your progress and achievements, so you won't have to start all over again. Happy days.

If you fancy giving any of these games a try this weekend, here's how to download and play them at no extra cost with your Xbox Game Pass subscription.

Just remember, you'll need an eligible Xbox Game Pass subscription, and the promotion ends at the end of this coming Sunday.

items.title: Path of Exile 2 Wants to Join Steam’s 1 Million Player Club With Version 1.0, As Grinding Gear Games Eyes Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077’s Records
items.summary: Path of Exile 2 director Jonathan Rogers aims to surpass 1 million Steam players when the free-to-play 1.0 launch hits
items.content:
While The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and Grand Theft Auto VI are monopolizing the attention of the entire video game industry, there are a few more highly anticipated games launching next month on PC , PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series X , and Xbox Series S . Chief among them is the official launch of Path of Exile 2 1.0 on December 11 , after two years in Early Access , a release that will mark the game's jump to a free-to-play model. Developer Grinding Gear Games' expectations for this launch are high, as they aim to reach a number of players on Steam that only eight games have to date.

"Our goal is to further expand the new player base through the 1.0 official launch and free-to-play transition. We have high expectations internally, especially since we heard that many existing 'Path of Exile' players are also eagerly awaiting the full launch of Path of Exile 2," said director Jonathan Rogers during a joint media interview in Busan, as reported by Inven Global . "To share a specific goal, we would love to surpass 1 million players on Steam. Of course, we also expect a significant number of players on other platforms. Considering Korean players as well, we believe even more people will enjoy the game."

Although it's not yet clear if Rogers meant concurrent players or total players, there's no denying that Path of Exile 2 has the potential to hit the 1 million concurrent players target on Steam , which is the hardest metric to hit, as it already hit 578,569 concurrent players on Steam on December 8, 2024, two days after its paid Early Access launch. With a free-to-play release, and many original Path of Exile players expected to make the jump, the game's concurrent players number is likely to be higher than the over half-a-million number of the Early Access release. For reference, only 8 games managed to do so so far, with two other major titles getting very close:

Alongside discussing the studio's player target, the Path of Exile 2 director addressed one of the community's biggest pain points: the length of the campaign and being forced to repeat it to level up alternate characters, among other things. While no campaign skip will be provided, new features will be introduced to alleviate the issues and enable speedier progress.

"The campaign focuses on enabling first-time players to fully experience the story and world while becoming immersed. Therefore, when playing through the campaign for the first time, we prepared it to preserve the classic story experience and the thrill of adventure," Rogers said. "However, we know that returning players or those replaying the campaign in a new league can feel fatigue from repeated play. To address this, we previously introduced features that more clearly guide players toward the next area or path. This improvement ensures that players repeating the campaign don't waste time finding their way and can progress faster. The previous Interlude content was temporarily prepared, so it fell short of the quality level the team aimed for. In contrast, the newly added Act 5 is official content built around a fresh storyline. We expect players to experience significantly higher quality and enjoyment compared to the previous Interlude."

Having only played Path of Exile 2 during gamescom 2024 and in its earliest Early Access incarnation , I am really looking forward to seeing how the entire experience has been overhauled for its official 1.0 launch. If the developer builds on the great qualities the game showed right from launch and keeps the momentum going by listening to community feedback, there's a high chance they will indeed reach that coveted player target.

About the author : Francesco De Meo has been covering video games and technology since 2012, starting his career at small outlets like Gamersyndrome and GeekSnack. items.title: GTA 6 bugs draw comparisons to Cyberpunk 2077's messy launch, but it's far from the same thing
items.summary: GTA 6 players have been encountering different bugs and glitches, and some are now comparing the launch to Cyberpunk 2077.
items.content:
PC Guide is reader-supported. When you buy through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Read More Table of Contents Latest tech deals. GTA 6 glitches spotted so far GTA 6 is finally here after more than a decade of waiting, and millions of players are getting their first taste of Rockstar Games’ massive open world. While the game has received excellent reviews, with an impressive record-tying score of 99 on Metacritic, some players have already started reporting bugs and glitches. A few of these issues have even led to comparisons with Cyberpunk 2077 , which had one of the most controversial launches in gaming history, and then one of the best redemptions.

🔥 More offers: see our Black Friday GTA 6 deals 2026 guide, updated daily, or browse all Black Friday deals .

However, it’s important to understand that GTA 6 is nowhere near as broken as Cyberpunk 2077 was when it first launched. The game has only just been released, and while there are some technical issues, the early reports don’t suggest that they are affecting the majority of players.

One of the clips getting attention comes from streamer Michael Does Life, who shared footage of a strange encounter with a police officer. During the fight, the characters appear to overlap with each other and even pass through nearby furniture. The streamer criticized the glitch and compared the situation to Cyberpunk 2077’s launch. Others show the player clipping out of the map.

GTA 6 is LITERALLY UNPLAYABLE because of this bug 😡 📽️ u/MyGothicAllure pic.twitter.com/mDjgTbNngp

Other players have also encountered unusual problems. For instance, streamer JasonTheWeen captured a large boat behaving strangely near a bridge, while another video shows Lucia apparently falling through the ground during a mission. There have also been reports of characters passing through objects and unexpected animations during police encounters.

JasonTheWeen discovers the first bug in GTA VI “I'm getting glitches and bugs already.. 13 years in the making” pic.twitter.com/d5Y4lglea8

Naturally, these clips have attracted plenty of attention on social media, especially considering how long Rockstar spent developing GTA 6. Some players expected the game to be nearly flawless at launch, while others have pointed out that occasional bugs are common in large open-world games. But comparing the situation to Cyberpunk 2077’s launch might be going too far.

When Cyberpunk 2077 arrived in December 2020, it suffered from widespread technical problems, particularly on older consoles. There’s a reason why GTA 6 isn’t on PS4 and Xbox One. Players reported serious performance issues, crashes, and numerous bugs that made the game difficult to enjoy. The situation became so bad that Sony temporarily removed Cyberpunk 2077 from the PlayStation Store and offered full refunds.

GTA 6, on the other hand, appears to be in a much better position. Although players have discovered glitches, the game has received overwhelmingly positive reviews, with critics praising its visuals, world design, and overall experience. There have been some performance concerns as well, particularly on the base PS5 , but the available evidence doesn’t suggest a launch disaster comparable to Cyberpunk 2077. Any full-on game crashes will likely remain the biggest concern for Rockstar with patches moving forward.

As a PC gamer, are you interested in upcoming consoles? Especially considering PC hardware prices?

I'll stick to gaming on PC for the foreseeable future

Abdul is a tech writer and Editor for PC Guide, specializing in all things tech, gaming, and hardware.

items.title: Check out what's coming to Cyberpunk 2077 in the Edgerunners 2 Update!
items.summary: Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you! Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watc
items.content:
Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you!

Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watch the Features Overview video to see some of the new features in action:

And if you want to know even more, read through the list of most important changes below:

Edgerunners Content

  • Added a new side quest, Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. To unlock it, complete The Heist and two gigs for Wakako, then wait for a message from her.

    [/*]

  • Added a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King, which can be obtained during the Clampdown side quest.

    [/*]

  • Added a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring a selection of tracks from the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners series.

    [/*]

Show Off

  • A brand-new clothing collection has arrived in Night City! 5 new outfit sets can now be purchased from certain clothing vendors:

    • Maxiwear: available in Heywood, Arroyo, Little China

      [/*]

    • Jinguji: available in City Center

      [/*]

    • NetWatch: available in Kabuki, Japantown

      [/*]

    • IconAmerica: available in Pacifica, Badlands, Northside

      [/*]

    • And one more set that will hit Night City shelves just a little later...

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • The NUS Infiltrator clothing set can be now purchased from clothing vendors in Kabuki and Japantown.

    [/*]

  • 4 new TWINTONE skins for Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech are now available via Twitch Drops.

    [/*]

  • Some of the hairstyles that were previously exclusive to NPCs are now available for V. Please note that some hairstyles are available only to feminine or masculine body types.

    [/*]

  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

    [/*]

  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.

    [/*]

  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.

    [/*]

  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

    [/*]

Mod the World

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.

    [/*]

  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

  • Saves in the “Load Game” menu are now grouped by separate playthroughs.

    [/*]

  • Added item filters to apartment and vehicle stashes.

    [/*]

  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several typos in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

    [/*]

items.title: The ‘Cyberpunk 2077’ Movie Will Expand the Game, Not Adapt It
Cyberpunk 2077 movie "won't be a one-to-one translation of the game's story", CD Projekt Red boss confirms, and boy do I think that's the right move
items.summary: CD Projekt Red joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski appears to have confirmed that the Cyberpunk 2077 movie won't be a straight-up adaptation of the game's story.
items.content:
A more Edgerunners-esque original tale from Night City looks to be in the offing

Image credit: CD Projekt News by Mark Warren Senior Staff Writer Published on Oct. 16, 2026, 3:15 p.m. 6 comments Follow Cyberpunk 2077 Since the existence of plans for a Cyberpunk 2077 live-action adaptation from devs CD Projekt Red and Paramount Pictures was revealed last week, I've been hoping it won't take the form of porting V's tale from the game to the big screen. Such a thing wouldn't necessarily be terrible, but I like my game adaptations a bit more on the original story side of things, as Cyberpunk tie-in anime series Edgerunners has been. The good news is that one of CD Projekt Red's big bosses has now confirmed that this adaptation won't be beat-for-beat retelling of 'Honey, there's a Keanu in my brain'.

There is a caveat in that the interview in question with CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski has been conducted and printed in Polish by business site PAP Biznes . A machine translation of the article suggests the exec said the following about the Cyberpunk movie:

"Our contract with Anonymous Content expired, and in the meantime, an opportunity arose to establish cooperation with Paramount Pictures, and we decided that we would conduct a live-action Cyberpunk project in a new formula. At this point, we can only say that we definitely don't want to make a film adaptation of the game. We want to tell a story in the world of Cyberpunk, but it won't be a one-to-one translation of the game's story."

Wary of relying solely on machine-translated quotes given they can result in meanings being twisted or made misinterpretable, we've run the quote by a Polish contact in order to try and root out any potential muddling of Nowakowski's words by the auto-translation. I've also reached out to CD Projekt Red for comment.

In a previous statement at the time the movie plans we confirmed, all Nowakowski said was that the studio are "excited about Paramount as a future partner who shares our creative ambitions for the Cyberpunk franchise" and would share more info on the film "at the appropriate time".

Assuming the movie does go the Edgerunners-esque route of telling a Night City story separate from the game's tale, that's definitely the right move in my eyes. Not only would that mean its creators don't have to agonise over how to make the pacing of an open-world game mesh with a film's runtime and could avoid having to decide how square messing with players' preferred headcanons about what V did or didn't do at various points, but it gives the creatives behind the film a chance to offer a fresher tale that perhaps explores some elements of the Cyberpunk world that the game didn't give as much attention to.

Then again, to avoid earning my ire, you've also got to avoid falling into the Fallout Season 2 trap of telling a fresh tale, but being desperate to hammer as many references to a game in as possible without conclusively advancing its setting in a way that makes the events of said game feel as meaningful it should. Basically, I'm saying I might be a bit too picky to be the ideal person to be trying to please with a game adaptation for the big screen.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 movie adaptation from Paramount on the way
items.summary: The smash hit from the studio behind The Witcher series is to be turned into a film by Paramount Pictures.
items.content:
Image source, CD Projekt Red Image caption, The Cyberpunk 2077 video game featured Keanu Reeves in one of the main roles

A live-action movie version of smash hit video game Cyberpunk 2077 is being developed by Paramount Pictures.

The Hollywood studio is working with producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura, known for his work on the Transformers films, and CD Projekt Red (CDPR), the developer of the sci-fi role-playing game.

CDPR's joint-chief executive Michał Nowakowski said in a statement , external the company was "excited about Paramount as a future partner who shares our creative ambitions for the Cyberpunk franchise".

Details of the film's story, potential release date and casting information are yet to be revealed.

Despite a troubled launch in 2020 , the Cyberpunk 2077 video game, which stars Keanu Reeves, has sold more than 40 million copies worldwide.

The John Wick star plays rockstar Johnny Silverhand, a terrorist whose consciousness is stored on a chip inside the body of main character V.

Set in Night City, a fictional metropolis in a dystopian version of California, players work to uncover a conspiracy involving the shady Arasaka megacorporation.

An expansion, Phantom Liberty, starring Idris Elba was released in 2023 and has sold more than 15 million copies, according to CDPR.

Cyberpunk has already been successfully adapted into a popular animated series - Edgerunners - with a second season due to premiere on Netflix later this month.

The streamer also produced The Witcher, an adaptation of CDPR's massively popular fantasy role-playing series.

It originally starred former Superman actor Henry Cavill, but he was replaced by Liam Hemsworth in the show's fourth season.

Image source, CD Projekt Red Image caption, Anime adaptation Cyberpunk: Edgerunners was a big hit with fans

Multiple video game series have been adapted for TV and film in recent years, with more due to follow.
